input: Get a full bloodwork panel done

keyUnknowns.whyItMatters: A 'full panel' means different things — basic metabolic, CBC, lipids, hormones, thyroid, vitamins, etc. Knowing which markers they want determines exactly what to request.
Whether a doctor is already involved (ordering the test) vs. the user going direct-to-consumer (e.g. Quest, LabCorp, private services) completely changes the path forward.
Is this routine/preventive, driven by specific symptoms, or for a condition they're already managing? The reason shapes which tests are prioritised and how urgently.
Whether they have health insurance, a budget cap, or no coverage determines which route (insurance-covered, employer benefit, or out-of-pocket direct-to-consumer) is viable.
Their location and access to labs or clinics determines which specific lab facilities or services to recommend and what prep (fasting, scheduling) is needed.
Some people want to interpret results themselves, others want a doctor to walk them through them — this affects whether to use a concierge service, a GP, or a telehealth provider.
Knowing what 'done well' looks like — e.g. having results in hand, understanding the numbers, or sharing them with a provider — defines where the task actually ends.

gold.taskTitle: Get a full bloodwork panel done
gold.taskDescription: The user wants to complete a comprehensive blood test, which involves deciding what tests to get, who orders them, where to go, and how to act on the results.

questions.title: Which specific markers do you want tested?
questions.description: Clarify whether the user wants a basic panel (CBC, metabolic) or an expanded one covering lipids, hormones, thyroid, vitamins, inflammatory markers, etc.

questions.title: Do you have a doctor who will order this?
questions.description: Determine whether the user has a primary care provider to write the order, or if they need to use a direct-to-consumer lab service.

questions.title: Is this routine, symptom-driven, or for a known condition?
questions.description: Understand the medical reason behind the request so the right tests and urgency level can be prioritised.

questions.title: Will you use insurance, or are you paying out of pocket?
questions.description: Identify the user's coverage situation to determine which service options (insurance lab, employer benefit, or self-pay services like Ulta Lab Tests) are realistic.

questions.title: What country or city are you located in?
questions.description: Pinpoint the user's location to suggest accessible lab facilities, walk-in options, or mail-in kits available to them.

questions.title: Do you want a professional to review your results with you?
questions.description: Find out if the user wants a doctor or clinician to interpret results, or if they prefer to review them independently.

questions.title: What does 'done' look like — results in hand, or action taken?
questions.description: Clarify whether the task ends when results are received, when they are understood, or when a follow-up action (e.g. medication, lifestyle change) has been decided.
